standard_prerequisites: the localization functor epsilon^* from D(O_X) to the small etale derived category over f^{-1}O_Y
tor amplitude of complexes over a morphism of ringed spaces, checked on stalks
stalks of pullback sheaves at geometric points and strict henselization
faithful flatness of henselization and its invariance for tor amplitude
core_obligations: Prove: (1) E over f^{-1}O_Y has tor amplitude in [a,b] iff epsilon^*E over f^{-1}O_{Y_etale} does; (2) locally finite tor dimension is likewise unchanged
proof_roadmap: The forward direction of (1) is the general tor-amplitude pullback lemma on sites

Fix a geometric point over x with y = f(x); compute the stalk of epsilon^*E as E_x derived tensor the strict henselization O_{X,x}^{sh} over O_{X,x}, using the identifications of the two pullback stalks
If epsilon^*E has tor amplitude in [a,b], its stalk has that amplitude over the strict henselization O_{Y,y}^{sh}; the henselization up-down lemma moves the amplitude to O_{Y,y}-modules

Faithful flatness of O_{X,x} to O_{X,x}^{sh} with the no-change tor amplitude lemma brings the amplitude back to E_x over O_{Y,y}; the stalkwise tor amplitude criterion gives (1) reversed, and (2) is formal from (1)
difficulty_reason: H2: a stalk-chase through strict henselization with two invariance lemmas; the source writes every identification out.
